A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RNA-FrameFlow, with matching methods, datasets, and retained experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original RNA backbone generation experiments, MMDiff comparisons, structural measurements, and loss and data-preparation ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds empirical pipeline calibration, forward-folding sensitivity, angular-distribution, and steric-clash analyses.

M1.justification: The RNA frames, eight torsions, IPA/Transformer architecture, flow-matching and auxiliary losses, and Euler sampling procedure are retained. Appendix A.4 documents the existing atom-reconstruction procedure more explicitly; it does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RNAsolo/PDB data, target backbone lengths of 40–150 nucleotides, and augmentation through longer-chain cropping. The added diagnostics reuse existing RNA populations and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds a 50/50 training-distribution reference baseline for local structural EMD. The original and retrained MMDiff comparators and Gaussian-noise baseline remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation protocols with training-half controls, natural-RNA pipeline calibration using 16 inverse-folded sequences, MSA-free Chai-1 evaluation, selected-length angular measurements, and normalized all-atom clash counts. It also states an alternative 4.3 Å RMSD validity threshold. Section 3 changes the reported optimizer and batch size from Adam/20 to AdamW/28 while retaining 120K steps; this does not establish reruns. The main benchmark still uses eight inverse-folded sequences.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of attainable self-consistency on natural RNAs, sensitivity to replacing RhoFold with Chai-1, detailed atomic bond-angle distributions, and quantitative steric clashes. These substantially broaden checks of evaluation reliability and physical realism. The earlier loss ablations, cropping/clustering studies, and RhoFold length-bias analysis are retained.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports numerical mean-plus/minus summaries, including valid-sample scTM of 0.641±0.161, scRMSD of 2.298±0.892, and clash counts. The meaning of the ± terms is not specified. The five-run sampling-time average already appears in v1; no additional training seeds or repeated-training counts are reported.

E6.justification: The main benchmark and existing ablation values are retained, including 41.0% validity for 50-step RNA-FrameFlow and 0.0% for MMDiff. Substantial new diagnostic results include the training-half EMD reference, natural-RNA FF and IF+FF self-consistency of 55.1% and 43.7%, Chai-1-based validity of 39.5%, and angular and clash measurements. These are added outcomes under additional evaluation conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 introduces an explicit mathematical definition of steric clashes using a van der Waals radius cutoff minus 0.6 Å, pairwise indicators, and their count. The core SE(3) interpolation, loss, and sampling equations are unchanged apart from regrouping and renumbering; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the claims of introducing RNA-FrameFlow for 3D RNA backbone generation, adapting protein flow matching to RNA, and generating 40–150-nucleotide backbones with over 40% validity. The abstract and conclusion preserve the same scientific scope and principal findings.

C2.justification: V2 explains that random crops may form unstable structures unfamiliar to evaluation models and interprets natural-RNA pipeline performance as a limit on measured validity. It also adds interpretations of folding-model sensitivity and clash similarity. The latter overstates agreement: Figure 16 and Appendix C.4 report substantially higher generated clash counts. Earlier generalization and physical-violation limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds atom-placement steps, bond/atom/torsion mappings, and OpenComplex as the source of idealized adenine bond lengths. Training documentation revises approximately 15 hours to 18 hours alongside the optimizer and batch-size changes. The architecture dimensions, hardware, and project code link are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting the new material, including Chai-1, Gelbin et al.'s geometry study, OpenComplex, and RNA-folding benchmarks. Positioning relative to FrameFlow, MMDiff, and RNAFlow remains substantially unchanged. The gRNAde citation changes to its 2025 publication rather than introducing a different work.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from v1 Appendix A to v2 Section 6, and the remaining appendices are reorganized with a contents page. Contribution and frame-rationale paragraphs receive limited rewriting, author/affiliation text changes, and acknowledgments are removed. Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document template, typography, margins, and title/header layout throughout. It adds Figures 7, 10, 15, and 16, an atom-placement diagram, and reference/mapping tables; expands Table 2; and introduces green result highlighting. Existing figures are retained but resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 improves assessment of the unchanged core findings through natural-data controls, Chai-1 sensitivity testing, quantitative atomic diagnostics, and additional reconstruction details. The gain is limited by overinterpretation: Appendix C.4 describes clash counts as similar despite reporting 25.55 versus 10.03 clashes per 100 atoms. The natural-RNA calibration also uses 16 inverse-folded sequences versus eight in the main benchmark, limiting direct comparison.
